_note: The arena's modes (docs/RESEARCH_PHASE_11.md sections 13 and 14). Team deathmatch: Apex is 6v6, first to 40, 10 minutes; the arena holds teams of up to 4, so ours is first to 30 (ours). Gun Run, Crown and Search were the legacy game's and went with it (the owner, 2026-10-04: "remove all legacy stuff").
_ffa: Free-for-all (ours; Apex has none, and the arena modes' shared rules give it for free): everyone for themselves in the arena, respawns, first to 20 kills or the most at 10 minutes, the fewest deaths on a tie, bots by the host's setting. A respawn picks the spot farthest from any enemy, as the other modes' do.
_control: Control (docs/RESEARCH_PHASE_12.md section 3), scaled to the arena: Apex plays 9 v 9 over three zones, 1 point a second per zone held, first to 1,000 or 30 minutes, a 150-point bonus zone, spawns on zones linked to your base, and a lockout when one team holds all three. Ours: 5 v 5, first to 500 or 10 minutes. The capture speed by the number on a zone is Apex's (1, 1.5, 2, 2.25, 2.5, 2.75, 3); the base capture time (8 s from neutral with one player, twice that to take an enemy's), the bonus timings, the lockout's 30 s and the 5 s respawn are ours (Apex's are unpublished, and it respawns in waves of up to 10 s). Zones are in arena coordinates: A on team A's side in the left lane, B in the middle, C on team B's side in the right lane.
_bots: bots added to a mode with no teams (free-for-all) by the host's setting; team deathmatch and Control fill both teams to teamSize. The cap is what the frame rate will carry rather than what the arena was drawn for: the owner asked to be able to put thirty and more in a match, to stress the game and to have something always shooting. Past the spawns a map has, they are stepped out around them in a grid.
_spawns: arena coordinates (the 1v1 arena's centre is 0, 0; team A's end is -z, team B's +z), each facing up the map toward the middle
_spawnFacing: Which way you face when an arena match puts you down. A spawn faces the middle, and the new arenas put a pillar or a container on that line on purpose, to break the shot from one spawn to the other; so a spawn faced the box a metre away. Now the facing turns, in steps of `step` degrees either side up to `sweep`, to the nearest heading with at least `clear` metres of open view, and keeps the middle when it already has that. Ours.
